thread:
Chris D.: quick heads-up: I hit a reproducible ESM/CJS interop that only shows up on the edge runner and it manifests as a 401 + missing function. repo: https://github.com/redwood-internal/repro-mixed-modules-edge (internal)
Chris D.: short summary: building the SDK + sampleapp with vite/esbuild or rollup+plugin-commonjs so that some deps are CJS -> deploy to edge -> outgoing SDK requests show `401` and runtime shows `TypeError: client.request is not a function`. ESM build works fine.
Yuki N.: interesting. is this specific to esbuild output or to any CJS output?
Chris D.: reproduced with 3 variants: (A) vite using esbuild bundle format 'cjs' + commonjsOptions.transformMixedEsModules=true, (B) rollup + @rollup/plugin-commonjs converting a dependency to CJS, (C) an esbuild-only build with `format: 'cjs'`. Webpack -> output: 'esm' didn't reproduce.
Marta G.: can you paste the minimal runtime error?
Chris D.: log from edge: 
```
ERROR: outgoing request failed: 401 Unauthorized
TypeError: client.request is not a function
    at file:///workspace/dist/index.js:72:20
    at async handleRequest (edge:internal)
```
Chris D.: repro steps (minimal):
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-internal/repro-mixed-modules-edge && cd repro-mixed-modules-edge
2) npm ci
3) npm run build:mix # builds a cjs-mixed bundle (vite/esbuild or rollup depending on script)
4) deno task start:edge (or deploy to edge runner)
5) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost/_invoke -> 401 + TypeError

Chris D.: vite config that reproduces it (minimal):
```js
// vite.config.js
export default {
  build: {
    lib: { entry: 'src/index.ts', formats: ['cjs'] },
    commonjsOptions: { transformMixedEsModules: true },
    target: 'es2020'
  }
}
```

Yuki N.: hunch: esbuild/rollup are wrapping the export shape (`module.exports = { default: ... }`) and the edge resolver then picks the CJS entry. That means callers expecting a default export end up with an object wrapper and the fetch wrapper doesn't get invoked as expected. Also check that `process.env` inlining or define plugins didn't remove the auth wrapper.
Marta G.: typings impact?
Chris D.: yep. TypeScript consumers that `import SDK from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` will still compile (if `esModuleInterop` is enabled locally) but break at runtime in strict projects. So DX friction is high — onboarding sample apps hitting CJS builds on edge will fail mysteriously.
edge-runner-bot: note: our edge deploy resolution prefers "main" when a CJS main exists. If the package.exports isn't set to prefer ESM, the edge runner will pick CJS.
Chris D.: short-term workarounds we validated: (1) Force ESM bundle output (formats: ['es']) for sample apps and SDK examples. (2) Add a tiny interoperability entry at package root that normalizes exports, e.g.: `const mod = require('./dist/cjs'); module.exports = mod && mod.__esModule ? mod.default : mod;` — ugly but works. (3) Prefer publishing an ESM-first package.json exports map so runtimes pick ESM.
Yuki N.: also tested rollup case: when plugin-commonjs converts a dep that contains a default export, rollup sometimes synthesizes `exports.default = whatever` which still ends up as a wrapper. We should document plugin settings to avoid mixing formats.
Marta G.: CI? can we add an integration smoke to catch this?
Chris D.: added a quick CI smoke job in the repro that builds three variants and runs a tiny edge emulation. build-bot: CI #7410 (mixed-modules-edge) finished  artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/repro/7410/
Marta G.: action items:
- Chris: add repro + CI job to devex docs and link in SDK issue.
- Yuki: draft a packaging recommendation (prefer ESM export, add exports map) and a tiny interop shim as a short-term patch.
- Platform: consider changing edge deployer to prefer module field when available (edge-runner maintainers), or at least warn when package main is CJS.
Chris D.: i'll open the PRs. added a short troubleshooting checklist to the repro README: check bundle format, check package.json exports/main/module, and run the small edge emulator locally. ping me for reviews. :thumbsup:
